title: Rapid triage rubric for intermittent air-gapped/on-prem upgrade requests
creator: Priya Shah
description: Context: Large enterprise customers regularly request staggered upgrades for private/VPC/on-prem Redwood deployments that are intermittently air-gapped (periodic maintenance windows with no external egress). These requests create two recurring problems: (1) high triage overhead and long SLA times when networking constraints are not documented consistently, and (2) risky ad-hoc engineering work during tight upgrade windows. Goal: Create a concise, repeatable triage rubric and routing lanes that lets the intake team score requests within 24 hours and either (A) auto-assign to a fast-track remediation play, (B) schedule a scoped engineering engagement, or (C) return a deterministic set of required customer actions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A 7-criteria scoring rubric documented on Confluence (network maturity, airgap window length, upgrade frequency, proxy/bridge availability, rollback ability, compliance constraints, customer business priority). 2) A mapping table that converts score ranges to routing lanes (self-serve checklist, PM-led engagement, engineering on-call + SRE). 3) A templated intake response email + required artifact checklist (network diagrams, firewall rules, upgrade window EST/UTC, console logs) that can be sent automatically from CRM. 4) Pilot with two enterprise customers and <48h triage SLA for 80% of incoming requests.
scope_inclusions: New private deploy upgrade requests, recurring upgrade scheduling requests, network-change impact assessments for on-prem customers, airgap exemption requests for security patches.
scope_exclusions: Bug reports, feature requests unrelated to deployment/networking, emergencies covered by incident on-call (use INC-xxxxx instead).
proposed_rubric_summary: Score fields and weights (total 100): Network Maturity (0-25) - validated by reachability tests and documented ACLs; Airgap Window Length (0-20) - <1h = 5, 1-4h = 12, >4h = 20; Upgrade Frequency Constraint (0-10) - once/year vs rolling monthly; Bridge/Proxy Availability (0-20) - presence of customer-managed proxy or edge connector; Rollback Complexity (0-10) - automated rollback vs manual steps; Compliance/Legal Blockers (0-10) - requires contract/legal signoff; Business Impact (0-5) - revenue-critical feature or not. Routing: 0-40 -> Self-serve checklist + prescriptive docs; 41-70 -> PM-led scoping + 2-week engineering window; 71-100 -> High-touch engineering SRE + dedicated upgrade runbook and on-site/remote support.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: - Keep rubric intentionally conservative to reduce mid-upgrade incidents; higher false-positive (more high-touch routing) acceptable in year 1. - Avoid building bespoke tooling initially; use score + manual gating by PM to reduce engineering churn. - For customers with strict airgap policies, prefer edge-connector pattern over transient egress when possible; will cost more but reduces upgrade risk.
operational_plays: 1) Self-serve lane: automated checklist + network probe script sent to customer; no engineering time expected. 2) PM-scoped lane: PM gathers artifacts, schedules a single 2-hour assessment with solutions engineer. 3) High-touch lane: ENG + SRE create a customer-specific runbook, validate proxies, schedule upgrade window, 1-day on-call during upgrade. 4) Emergency exemption path: separate incident process; requires security review and exec signoff.
estimated_engineering_effort: Fast-track scripts and templates: 8h; Confluence + email automation templates: 6h; Pilot engagement with two customers (supporting): 24h total engineering + 12h SRE; Documentation & training: 10h.
customer_message_template: Thank you for your private-deploy upgrade request. To triage we ask you to complete the attached network probe and upload your firewall rules, upgrade window (start/end in UTC), and whether a customer-managed proxy/edge-connector is available. Based on these inputs our intake team will respond within 24 hours with one of: (A) self-serve checklist, (B) scheduled scoping call, (C) high-touch upgrade runbook. If your environment is strictly air-gapped please indicate the last window you permitted egress and whether offline media/USB transfer is an option.
pilot_plan: Week 0: finalize rubric and checklist. Week 1: pilot with Customer A (financial services) to validate scoring thresholds. Week 2: adjust weights and pilot with Customer B (healthcare). Week 3: finalize automated intake email and handoff to support. Measure: triage SLA, number of engineering-hours per request.
risks: - Customers may under-report network constraints leading to mid-upgrade failures. Mitigation: require network probe output as gating artifact. - High-touch lane could create scheduling bottlenecks if many requests score >70. Mitigation: cap high-touch commits/month and offer dedicated paid engagement. - Legal/compliance delays for regulated customers. Mitigation: early Legal gating in scoring.
next_steps: 1) Review rubric with Solutions Engineering and SRE (by 2025-02-14). 2) Build network probe script and attach to intake email (by 2025-02-21). 3) Create Confluence doc and intake automation in Zendesk/CRM (by 2025-02-28). 4) Run pilot with two customers and iterate (by 2025-03-14).
